main_body: A flat ground patch of brick-like paving, 4x3 tiles, with cream and pink-grey bricks, grey mortar lines and a few blue-grey and dark-green strips. It is not a standing object.
top_band: none. This is a flat terrain pattern, so the column scan shows repeating brick courses (cream L=187, pink-grey L=178, mid L=145, mortar L=86), not a top band over a front face.
evidence: The kind is terrain, so the standing-object contract (top band plus front face) does not apply. The drawing is a flat tiling surface with no standing volume, no receding side faces and no object standing on it. Nothing in it breaks the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The candidate has 11 colours and a median of 7 per tile, which equals the paving reference (7 and 7) and is far below the grass reference (26 and 80). Flat-fill coverage is 0%, as in both references. The bricks carry about 5 steps (cream, pink-grey, mid brown-grey, dark mortar, light grey) with speckle and per-brick variation. Mortar and dark edges are partly neutral grey (30% neutral), and the paving reference is similar, at 80%. The blue-grey and dark strips are a little odd, but they add variation rather than flat areas. At the same scale it would sit acceptably next to the paving reference, though it is simpler than the grass.
